admission.justification: A future classifier must not promote locator repair alone into meaning change or hide it merely because it fixes evidence already stale at base.

alternatives.option: Classify a nonmechanical stale-entry reanchor as implementation evidence, separately from recorded invariant meaning.
alternatives.reason: Appendix151 explicitly separates reanchoring from meaning. _ChangeKinds._entry_changes consults the base class and carried_mechanically before establishing re-anchored implementation; _intent delegates recorded meaning to its independent owner.

alternatives.option: Treat an anchor repair alone as an invariant meaning change, or discard it merely because the old entry was stale.
alternatives.reason: An evidence locator is not the obligation text, and a stale-at-base repair is still deciding implementation work under the admitted classifier.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The invariant meaning actually changes alongside the repair, or an approved requirement changes the explicit implementation-versus-intent classification contract.

consequences: A future classifier must not promote locator repair alone into meaning change or hide it merely because it fixes evidence already stale at base.
A purely mechanical carry can be ignored by carried_mechanically; an unreadable base class remains unknown; a concurrent actual invariant-text change is not declared unchanged.
context: Approved MIK-R57@v2 appendix83/151 and rule6 require this by-design choice to be recorded, not deferred as a gap. Source obligation: MIK-R57@v2 by-design reanchor. This is the requirement-prescribed boundary, not a claim that an undocumented alternative was seriously weighed.
decider: Approved MIK-R57@v2 under D18/D47/D48; Curator records the specified boundary under constrains_future_work.
